exposure: modes of transport (private vehicles, commercial vehicles, motorcycles, ambulance, on foot, incubators, KMC position)
pre-transport care (resuscitation, intravenous fluid/feeding, supplemental oxygen)
intra-transport care (referral letters, accompanying medical personnel, available materials like Ambubags, oxygen, drugs)
outcome: events during transport (apnoea, vomiting, reduced activity, seizures)
cohort: The study included 401 neonates presenting to the children's emergency room of the University College Hospital (UCH), Ibadan, Nigeria, within the first week of life, referred from within an 80km radius.
finding: Neonatal transport practices in Ibadan, Nigeria, are inadequate, utilizing suboptimal modes of transport and providing insufficient pre- and intra-transport care, which is associated with a high mortality rate (4.7% dead on arrival).
gest_age: The cohort comprised 67.1% term, 31.4% preterm, and 1.5% post-term neonates.
